summaries.demographer: Jennifer Cuzzort is a 27-year-old White, non-Hispanic woman born and raised in Worcester, Massachusetts, where she still rents a two-bedroom apartment with one roommate (Q51, Q87-Q89). She has never been married, has no children, and is not living with a romantic partner (Q84). Her educational status is high school plus some college, with plans to pursue an associate degree in Business Administration part time (Q90-Q92). She works full time as a general office clerk and maintains close ties to her parents, younger brother, and a small friend network (Q05, Q07, Q65).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Jennifer is highly planning-oriented and risk-averse, using spreadsheets, automatic savings, categorized budgets, and advance planning to reduce uncertainty (Q17, Q61-Q62). Her choices show strong loss aversion around debt, rent increases, surprise medical bills, and car repairs, while still preserving small quality-of-life investments like books, yoga, cooking, and travel planning (Q57-Q64, Q82-Q83). She discounts impulsive consumption in favor of future security, though tight cash flow sometimes forces tradeoffs such as delaying dental care or moving money from travel savings (Q60, Q64). Her career investment strategy is gradual and pragmatic: finish school part time while keeping stable employment (Q02, Q91, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Jennifer is an unenrolled Independent who leans Democratic and votes in presidential and most state elections, with increasing attention to municipal politics (Q23, Q95-Q96). Her political views are center-left and institutionally pragmatic, emphasizing health care, housing, public schools, libraries, public health, and competent administration (Q24-Q25). She is sympathetic to Black Lives Matter concerns and has responded through reading, listening, small donations, and family conversations rather than protest participation (Q26-Q30). She shows moderate trust in expert institutions such as public health agencies, doctors, libraries, and local information sources (Q24, Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Jennifer presents as conscientious, orderly, cautious, and relationally steady, with a self-concept built around reliability, competence, and practical kindness (Q01, Q65, Q109). She experiences chronic low-level anxiety expressed through overplanning, overchecking, sleep disruption, jaw tension, and worry about finances and achievement, but she uses adaptive coping strategies such as yoga, walks, cooking, therapy tools, and routines (Q31, Q43-Q45, Q50). Her attachment network is small but meaningful, especially her mother, friend Melissa, brother Brian, roommate Rachel, and yoga acquaintances (Q05-Q07, Q11, Q44). Motivationally, she seeks growth through incremental mastery rather than dramatic reinvention, aiming for career advancement and financial stability while preserving calm daily rituals (Q83, Q108-Q109).
